faults.fault: In the 1.8x wider and 1.7x taller renders the cabinet/background texture is badly streaked and banded -- smeared vertical runs down the right of the wide version and mirrored blotch bands down the whole lower half of the tall version. A player can point straight at it.

The widened machine (image 3) gained NO product columns: the window still shows the original three columns and the extra width went into blank smeared panel on both sides. A wider vending machine must show more bays in the window, with the frame stretching to hold them.
Price/product decals did not multiply with the width and the price text is cut to a stray '1.0' fragment in the widened render -- stretched/cut text is blocking.
The tallened machine (image 4) gained no extra shelf row of products; the extra height is blank streaked cabinet between the window and the flap instead of another tier inside the window.

A thin flat slab stands proud off the upper-left edge of the body (visible in images 2, 4 and 5 as a floating flap-like panel beside the marquee), reading as a bug rather than a door or a trim member.

At 1.7x tall the prop has gained a repeat it did not have when drawn: its row profile self-correlates 1.00 at a period of 76 scanlines, against 0.38 at the drawn size. Something is being laid down more than once.

wider_means: A wider vending machine has more product columns in the display window, with the cabinet body, coin station and dispenser flap stretching to match.
taller_means: A taller vending machine has another shelf row of products inside the window plus extra plain cabinet panel between the window, the dispenser flap and the base.
